utterance: Hi there, I'm so glad you're here. I'm really looking forward to getting to know you and hearing what's on your mind today. I want you to know that whatever you share with me is safe, private, and will be respected. How are you feeling right now? What brings you in today?

Hi, thanks for having me here. I’ve been feeling kind of stuck lately—like I’m not sure what’s really going on. I wake up every morning and my body just feels… off. I can’t sleep properly, and when I finally do fall asleep, I’m not sure if I’m actually resting. My legs hurt when I’m lying down, and sometimes I feel like I’m going to pass out—dizzy, like the room is spinning. I don’t know if it’s just stress or something deeper, but I’ve been avoiding school for a while now because the thought of waking up just feels too scary. I’m not sure where to start, but I think it’s time to talk about it. What do you think?

The dizziness, the leg pain, the way your body reacts when you think about waking up—it all makes school feel impossible. I can see how avoiding it might seem like the only way to protect yourself from the panic. I’m here to listen, and I wonder if it might be helpful to look more closely at what’s happening when you’re trying to get up. Would you feel comfortable exploring that with me?

It feels really hard to even start—like I’m holding my breath just to keep from falling apart. The leg pain and dizziness don’t just happen when I wake up; they come on strong the moment I try to move. I don’t know if it’s the fear or something deeper, but every time I think about getting out of bed, my heart jumps and my stomach flips. I’m scared I’ll just collapse. But… I think I’d want to explore it, if you’re okay with me taking it slow. Maybe we could start with just noticing what happens when I try to sit up in the morning?

The leg pain comes first, then the dizziness, and suddenly I’m gripping the edge of the bed, heart pounding, trying not to panic. Even just noticing what happens in the quiet moments before I have to move. Would that be okay?
